title: Utility and energy-assistance screens precede distinct but uncertain next-month work changes
source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use file, 2024 reference year; identified person-month pairs

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility-payment screen at month t and following-month work measures

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs with valid household-status, utility field, positive weight, and consecutive months; outcome measures retain their own valid pair counts

observations.method: Same-person monthly transition: valid EAWBGAS utility-payment screen at month t, then nonnegative numeric TPEARN and TMWKHRS change at month t+1; WPFINWGT from month t and 240 Census replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5. THHLDSTATUS and AAWBGAS validity filters retained.
observations.uncertainty: Approximate Fay-BRR intervals are wide for the utility-difficulty hours-change estimate. Earnings and hours have separate valid-pair universes; person-month rows repeat household fields and are not a household-prevalence estimate.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting utility-payment difficulty at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: The high earnings-change share does not mean utility difficulty caused earnings movement; monthly earnings can change for seasonal, job, demographic, or reporting reasons. Hours movement is imprecise in this subgroup.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility-payment difficulty at month t and following-month work measures

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs with valid household-status, utility field, positive weight, and consecutive months; outcome measures retain their own valid pair counts

observations.method: Same-person monthly transition using the same SIPP fields, validity rules, WPFINWGT, and 240-replicate Fay-BRR procedure as the utility-difficulty comparison.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is descriptive and uses separate valid universes for earnings and hours. The no-difficulty hours estimate is more precise than the difficulty estimate but does not identify a causal contrast.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting no utility-payment difficulty at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower hours-change share without reported utility difficulty does not establish that utility stability protects work continuity; job composition, seasonality, and selection into the reported utility field may differ.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; energy assistance at month t and following-month work measures

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs with valid energy-assistance field, positive weight, and consecutive months; outcome measures retain their own valid pair counts

observations.method: Same-person monthly transition using EENERGY_ASST code 1, WPFINWGT, and the 240-replicate Fay-BRR procedure.
observations.uncertainty: Energy-assistance status is a reported field with its own missingness and selection. The estimate describes a conditional transition surface, not assistance effectiveness or work displacement.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: Assistance may be targeted to households already facing work or health instability; the lower earnings-change share could reflect composition or support, and the data do not distinguish those explanations.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no energy assistance at month t and following-month work measures

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs with valid energy-assistance field, positive weight, and consecutive months; outcome measures retain their own valid pair counts

observations.method: Same-person monthly transition using EENERGY_ASST code 2, WPFINWGT, and the 240-replicate Fay-BRR procedure.
observations.uncertainty: The no-assistance comparison retains the field-specific valid universes and does not control for income, tenure, season, health, household composition, or job type.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting no energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: Differences between assistance and no-assistance groups may reflect eligibility, need, geography, or reporting selection rather than a protective or disruptive effect of assistance.

related_sources.claim: Official SIPP field definitions, codes, universes, and status flags.
Official 240-replicate-weight archive used for Fay-BRR variance.

boundary: This is a same-person, month-to-next-month descriptive SIPP transition screen. It places utility-payment difficulty and energy-assistance status beside subsequent earnings and hours movement, but it does not observe the exact bill, work shock, desired hours, care substitution, remedy, recovery, trust, political action, or a causal effect of utility conditions or assistance. Person-month rows repeat household fields and are not household prevalence estimates.
